label: 1929 Crash
cause: Wall Street Crash: a speculative bubble built on borrowed money burst (Black Thursday and Black Tuesday, October 1929).

label: Great Depression
cause: Bank failures, deflation, tight money and the Smoot-Hawley tariffs turned the crash into a worldwide depression.

label: 1933 banking panic
cause: A new wave of bank runs, ending in the national bank holiday of March 1933.

label: 1933 rally unwinds
cause: The speculative rally after the dollar left the gold standard collapsed, amid doubts about the New Deal's recovery programme.

label: Stalled recovery
cause: An uneven recovery from the Depression and uncertainty about New Deal policies and new market regulation.

label: 1937–38 recession
cause: The Fed doubled banks' reserve requirements and the government cut spending, pushing the economy back into recession.

label: War fears in Europe
cause: The growing threat of war in Europe; Germany occupied Czechoslovakia in March 1939.

label: WWII: fall of France
cause: World War II: Germany's invasion of Western Europe and the fall of France (May–June 1940).

label: WWII: Pearl Harbor
cause: World War II: the attack on Pearl Harbor (December 1941) brought the US into the war, followed by early Allied defeats.

label: Post-war inflation
cause: The end of wartime price controls: an inflation surge, strikes and fears of a post-war slump.

label: 1948–49 recession
cause: Tighter money against post-war inflation, followed by the 1948–49 recession.

label: 1957 recession
cause: Fed rate rises, the 1957–58 recession and the Sputnik shock (October 1957).

label: Kennedy Slide
cause: High valuations unwound; President Kennedy's clash with the steel industry and the flash crash of May 1962.

label: 1966 credit crunch
cause: Inflation rose with Vietnam War and Great Society spending, and the Fed tightened credit sharply.

label: 1969–70 recession
cause: Rising inflation and interest rates, the Vietnam War and the 1969–70 recession (Penn Central's collapse in 1970).

label: Oil crisis & stagflation
cause: The OPEC oil embargo (1973), stagflation, the end of the Bretton Woods system, Watergate and the end of the 'Nifty Fifty' boom.

label: Volcker rate shock
cause: The Fed (Paul Volcker) raised interest rates to about 20% to break inflation, causing the 1981–82 recession.

label: Black Monday
cause: The S&P 500 fell 20.5% on 19 October 1987 alone: high valuations, rising rates and automated 'portfolio insurance' selling.

label: Dot-com bubble
cause: The internet/tech bubble burst, followed by the 2001 recession, the 9/11 attacks and accounting scandals (Enron, WorldCom).

label: Global financial crisis
cause: The US housing and subprime-mortgage bubble burst; Lehman Brothers' collapse (September 2008) set off a global banking crisis.

label: COVID-19 pandemic
cause: The COVID-19 pandemic and lockdowns: the fastest fall into a bear market on record.

label: Inflation & rate hikes
cause: High inflation and the fastest Fed rate rises since the 1980s; Russia's invasion of Ukraine (February 2022) added an energy shock.
